Discriminates true/false only partially as written. Defects: (1) LEGALITY GAP: chi(R+[a]P)=chi(R)chi([a]P); the phase chi(R) is a function of log R, so choosing a to hit a peak needs DL information (for prime r, all of it). 'Peak-chosen offset' in a full-DL-table toy silently uses the secret and gives an illegal upper bound; a legal selector can only probe yields at m offsets (m oracle calls) and pick the best, which is a sinusoid-phase search whose gain is at most 1+(|hat|/B)^k, i.e. constant unless |hat|/B stays Omega(1). (2) Control is stated only for the max statistic: max|hat|/sqrt(B) for random B-subsets already grows like sqrt(log r) with n, and B and r both grow with n, so fitting B^c with c>0.1 over a 5-point range conflates the two; one extreme statistic is noisy. (3) Cofactor/small-order character artefact: binary curves have cofactor 2/4 and halving (Tr(x)=Tr(a2) iff point in 2E) makes Tr-hyperplane subspace bases land in a single coset, giving |hat|=B for the order-2/4 characters; prime-field curves of prime order avoid it. Such hits are the known halving/twist structure (closed), not prime-order r spectral structure, and would produce a false 'survives'. (4) Poisson floor: when B^k/r<1 the yield variance of a random base is ~mean, so 'variance' must be reported as excess over Poisson/random-set expectation. (5) Scaling: toy tests only the null (spectral flatness of DL-image of structured sets); that is a pseudorandomness question already closed in the atlas (DL character-sum pseudorandomness; coordinate-statistic bias hunts exhausted at scale; Kohel-Shparlinski). A flat result at n<=17-20 is consistent with but does not prove flatness at n=131; it can only exclude a mechanism that predicts B^{c} growth already visible at toy B. Even a positive result is engineering unless |hat|/B stays constant with n, and per brief rule 5 variance of yield does not move B*D^2 vs N. Classification if true: constant-factor (engineering).
fix: Redesign. (A) Spectrum arm, exact and cheap: for each curve (prime p in 2^16..2^22 with prime group order via cypari2 ellcard; binary n=13..20 with cofactor stripped by mapping base points through [h] into the prime-order subgroup and discarding identity) build full DL table by iterated addition (numpy/int arrays; <=2^22 adds), indicator f on Z/r, spectrum via numpy.fft. For each shape (affine F_2-subspace of coordinates, interval of x-integers, multiplicative subgroup of F_q*, Hamming ball, cyclotomic/trace-spectrum set) and each B in a geometric grid, compute: M=max_{chi!=0}|hat|/sqrt(B), E4=sum_{chi!=0}|hat|^4/r (additive energy excess), and Ek=sum|hat|^{2k} for k=2,3. Report z-scores against N>=200 matched controls: (i) uniformly random B-subsets of Z/r, (ii) same base with the DL table replaced by a random permutation of Z/r (same B, same structure in coordinates, DL structure destroyed), (iii) random base of the same shape under a random affine reparametrisation of coordinates. Primary statistic is ratio shape/control median with bootstrap CI, plotted against log2 B at fixed n and against n at fixed B/r exponent; prediction_if_true is ratio growing with log B (slope>0, CI excluding 0), prediction_if_false is ratio=1 within CI at every cell. Use Ek excess over Poisson floor, not raw variance. (B) Exact yield arm: yield Y_k(t)=k-fold cyclic convolution of f via FFT (ordered tuples; subtract diagonal terms for distinct-element yield at k=2,3), for all t in Z/r. Report Var_t(Y_k)/mean(Y_k) (Fano factor) vs control, and check Parseval identity Var=sum|hat|^{2k}/r^2 numerically as a self-test. (C) Selection arm, legal vs illegal: for random target R, (a) ORACLE: a*=argmax_a Y_k(log R + a) using the known log R (upper bound, labelled illegal); (b) BLIND-m: probe m=4,8,16,32 offsets, take best, report the mean Y of the chosen offset vs best-of-m of random offsets under the control (equal oracle-call budget), i.e. gain_blind/gain_control; also the regression of Y_k on a to show sinusoid at the peak frequency. Success quantity: gain factor G(n)=E[Y chosen]/E[Y mean]; prediction_if_true G grows with n at fixed B^k/r; false G=1+o(1) and the blind arm indistinguishable from best-of-m control. (D) Add a positive control: plant a base with a prescribed bias (take B points whose DL lies in an interval of Z/r of width r/4 mixed 50:50 with random) to show the pipeline detects |hat|/B=Omega(1) and measures the legal-selector gain; this calibrates what a 'true' outcome looks like. (E) Extend toy to prime p~2^24 (FFT size 2^24 complex128 ~256MB) only if time allows; fit log(ratio) vs n and report slope with CI so the n=131 statement is 'toy slope s+-e, mechanism requires s>0; extrapolated ratio at n=131 is X only if s significant'. Do not claim anything about n=131 beyond the slope. Counts only (characters, yields, oracle probes); no wall time. Cost estimate with fix ~12-18 CPU-minutes.
